title: Intro to Clone Paint and History Select 2021 — Post-processing workflow with history-based painting and clone-paint techniques

date.basis: Embedded creation_time metadata suggests 2021-02-22; transcript does not independently confirm the date.

summary: This instructional video outlines a photographer’s post-processing workflow centered on selective exposure management, dynamic range balancing, and painterly editing achieved through two parallel image variants. The speaker demonstrates adjusting exposure and dynamic range, adding directional light via dodging, and performing tonal- and color-based color grading in RAW/Camera Raw before painting those adjustments into a second RAW version in Photoshop. A core feature is the clone-paint workflow, where adjustments from a copied image are painted onto the original using a clone-stamp approach, contrasted with the history-brush method. The video also covers texture work (via cloning), foliage enhancement with the sponge tool, and a non-destructive mindset that emphasizes saving multiple versions to preserve options.

sections.title: Image selection and initial exposure balancing
sections.description: The presenter previews the selection of trip images and explains beginning post-processing by lowering exposure and using the dynamic range panel to raise lights while restoring blacks and shadows, aiming for a view closer to eye perception.

sections.title: Color grading concepts: tonal-based vs color-based adjustments
sections.description: Discussion on differentiating tonal-based adjustments (e.g., luminosity-driven changes) from color-based adjustments (targeting specific color ranges). The speaker demonstrates adjusting color temperature, tint, and introduces camera calibration as a tool, cautioning about banding with wide HSL edits.

sections.title: Photoshop workflow intro: two-image approach and blending without selections
sections.description: The workflow concept is introduced: create a second RAW version to pull adjustments from, plan to blend by painting rather than using selections, and prepare to move these adjustments into Photoshop.

sections.title: History Brush-based painting and RAW adjustments in Photoshop
sections.description: The speaker uses Camera Raw Filter to craft light adjustments on a second variant, then applies them with the History Brush to paint warmth and direction onto the primary image, emphasizing a painterly, non-destructive workflow and the avoidance of hard selections.

sections.title: Clone Painting workflow: sampling from a copy and painting onto the original
sections.description: An extended demonstration of clone painting: duplicating the image to preserve history, aligning the copies, and using the clone stamp to transfer texture and color from the copy to the original while selectively masking. The process includes texture work in shadows and preliminary cloud/fog texture adjustments, plus a note on using the sponge tool for foliage.

sections.title: Non-destructive saving and final notes
sections.description: The video closes with guidance to save multiple versions to safeguard past states and maintain flexibility, highlighting a non-destructive editing philosophy.

featured_techniques.technique: Dynamic range balancing using exposure and the dynamic range panel (blacks/shadows and whites/highlights)
Directional side lighting through dodging to enhance perceived light direction
Tonality-based vs color-based color adjustments; color grading with color wheel and luminosity controls
Camera Calibration tool for global color adjustment and color harmony
History Brush as primary adaptive painting workflow for applying adjustments
Clone Painting workflow: duplicating the image and painting from the copy onto the original using clone stamp
Sponge Tool for selective foliage color and saturation adjustments
Non-destructive versioning and saving multiple states to preserve edits
